title: Never made enough money; moving to California
summary: He dismisses the reported $1,750 a week in vaudeville and says he moved west because Los Angeles paid more and had sunshine.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: make enough money in these films or

I didn't make enough money in nothing. Never made enough money in nothing. From the time I started. Best most money I got, when I won the first prize Amateur Night for what I did, to get $50 I think, okay. I was able to do a dance and a song, I should have got more money than that.
I recall reading in Jazz Dance, Marshall Sterns book about you receiving $1750.00 a week in vaudeville.

Yeah, that ain't no money. That ain't no money, though. You're talking about money. That ain't no money. $1750? How do you think Frank Sinatra's rich? He ain't (inaudible) sing as much as I have. I've been in the business before he was born. So what are you going to do about that? What do you do about Sammy Davis? Look at the money that Sammy Davis is making now, we're not trying

to take away from his ability, we're taking him from the time he's doing his act, the time he goes on the stage, the time he goes off four times as much money as I made. That's why I'm in California, that's why I was out here. Because New York wasn't paying no money comparing when you come out here you get five thousand and ten thousand dollars a week for what they do and I'm doing four times as much in New York for quarter, I might as well come out here where they can get me cheaper than them other actors such as Harry Belafonte, Sidney Poitier and Sammy Davis, Jr., and Lena Horne. And I had as much talent as all those there, so why should I sell it for a quarter when I can get a dollar and a quarter for it right here. That's what brought me out here, plus the sunshine. That's something to think about, the sunshine, I've been looking at that all along. It was hard to get out here and find a place to live. See what I mean? Now, what have you got to say?
